points.description: States that infinite recursion can be caused by a missing base case, i.e. the function has no terminating/base case condition that stops the recursive calls.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if a base case is mentioned but the statement is imprecise (e.g. says base case is wrong/never reached without saying it is missing).

points.description: States that infinite recursion can be caused by an incorrectly defined recursion step, i.e. the recursive call does not move the argument/problem toward the base case.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only says the recursive call is 'wrong' without stating that it fails to progress toward the base case.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both causes stated precisely with correct terms: missing base case, and an incorrect recursion step (not progressing toward the base case). Each cause is worth half the marks; a vague or merely implied statement (e.g. 'the function keeps calling itself') earns nothing for that point. A wrong extra cause stated as a cause (e.g. 'too many variables') costs the point it conflicts with; answers giving only one cause get at most 2.5.
